content.text:
Only Li8VO6 (mp-1176805) matches the pattern; I found no evidence of a second phase.

- **Li8VO6:** it is the only candidate whose simulated peaks fall where the observed ones do: about 17.5, 19.9, 22.5, 36.1, 49.3, 55.5 and 64 degrees, among others. Fitted alone it gives R ≈ 0.65.
- **The other eight:** fitted alone, each gives R ≈ 0.98–1.03. That means they explain essentially none of the pattern.
- **Residual after the Li8VO6 fit:** it still has peaks of up to about 27 (on the 0–100 scale), so the fit is not clean. But at every observed peak the residual swings negative, then positive, then negative. That pattern comes from a small mismatch in peak position or width, not from extra peaks. I did not see any leftover peak that would need another phase, though I did not run a two-phase fit to confirm.

{"present": ["mp-1176805"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "Li8VO6 is the only candidate whose peak positions match the observed pattern (R 0.65 vs about 1.0 for all others), and its residual has only peak-shape mismatches, not unexplained peaks from a second phase."}
